newsitem.title: INDIA: India court grants bail to former federal minister.
newsitem.headline: India court grants bail to former federal minister.

text.p: India's highest court on Thursday granted bail to a former federal minister convicted by a special court of sheltering six people wanted by police.

The Supreme Court directed that Kalpnath Rai, food minister in the previous Congress government of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, be released on bail after he furnished a personal bond of 100,000 rupees and two sureties of the same amount.
Rai was directed not to leave the country without prior permission of the court that sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment and a fine of one million rupees ($27,932).
Rai challenged the decision to imprison him in India's Supreme Court, which ordered his release.

"The appeal is admitted...in the meanwhile the appellant (Kalpnath Rai) is to be released on personal bond of 100,000 and two sureties of like amount to the satisfaction of the designated court," the court said in its order.
Trials in cases registered under India's Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, which has now lapsed, are conducted by special courts set up for the purpose.

But cases launched when the law was in force are still being tried under the law. The law was allowed to lapse in 1995, ten years after it was enacted, following widespread protests from human rights activists who called it draconian.
